questions.question: Describe how you would use red and blue litmus paper to decide whether a solution is acidic, neutral or basic.
questions.expected_answer: Touch the solution onto both papers with a clean glass rod. If blue litmus turns red, it is acidic. If red litmus turns blue, it is basic. If neither changes, it is neutral.

questions.question: A solution turns universal indicator blue. State its approximate pH and classify it, and give an example of such a substance.
questions.expected_answer: About pH 8 to 10; a weak base. Example: bicarbonate of soda solution or soap solution.

questions.question: Explain how to make red cabbage indicator and state its colour in an acid, in water and in a base.
questions.expected_answer: Chop red cabbage, soak in hot water for about 10 to 15 minutes, strain and keep the purple liquid. Acid: pink to red; water: purple; base: blue-green to green (yellow in a very strong base).
